section.title: Using a Professional Indexer
section.p: Professional indexers Authorsas indexers Some authors may be tempted to save money by employing a family member or a graduate student to prepare the index. Others may even consider writing the index themselves. In both cases, this is usually a bad idea. It is rare for anyone to have the native ability to create a good index without training and experience.

Indexingskills required Professional indexers have developed specific skills including the ability to identify indexable concepts, select appropriate access points, create effective cross-reference structures, and use dedicated indexing software efficiently.

section.title: Finding an Indexer
section.p: Advertising to find indexers American Society of Indexers (ASI)Index Locator and Jobs Hotline There are several ways to find a qualified indexer. Personal referrals from colleagues are often the best approach. Internet searches can also be productive. The American Society of Indexers (ASI) maintains an Index Locator directory where editors can search for indexers by subject specialty and geographic location.

section.title: Indexer Qualities
section.p: Indexer qualifications Budget for indexes, indexer qualifications and When evaluating potential indexers, consider their experience with similar types of material, their familiarity with the subject area, their references, and their demonstrated ability to meet deadlines. Budget considerations should not lead to selecting an unqualified indexer.
